comparison_assessments.accuracy_note: The lyric preserves the comparison to a planted tree beside watercourses, fruit produced in its season, unwithered foliage, and success in whatever the person does. The literal rendering follows the same sequence and retains the Hebrew's connecting conjunctions more explicitly.
comparison_assessments.creative_liberties_note: “Bearing” idiomatically expresses giving fruit. “When its season comes” expands “in its season” without materially changing the timing. “Leaves” naturally represents the collective singular. The lyric drops several conjunctions and uses “thrive” for success, echoing the surrounding tree imagery.

word_notes.lexical_gloss: Prosper, succeed; cause to prosper, bring to a successful outcome.
word_notes.note: Conveys flourishing success and sustains the botanical resonance. It still applies to whatever the person does, rather than adding a separate claim about the tree.

comparison_assessments.accuracy_note: Preserves the tree image, deliberate planting, fruitfulness, enduring foliage, and a general picture of flourishing, in the Hebrew's order.
comparison_assessments.creative_liberties_note: Turns a third-person comparison into a direct-address metaphor. Eden replaces streams of water; freshness and monthly fruiting are supplied. Unwithering foliage becomes never dropping a leaf, and success in everything the person does becomes perpetual blossom.

literal_backbone: And he will be like a tree planted beside streams of water,
which yields its fruit in its season,
and its leaf does not wither; / and all that he does will prosper.

word_notes.note: The verb can describe transplanting, so replanting is a defensible choice.

word_notes.lexical_gloss: Beside streams or channels of water.
word_notes.note: Eden is not named; its introduction replaces the explicit water-source image.

word_notes.lexical_gloss: It gives its fruit at its time or in its season.
word_notes.note: Bearing fruit is preserved, but freshness is added and seasonal timing becomes an unsupported monthly schedule.

word_notes.lexical_gloss: And its leaf or foliage does not wither or fade.
word_notes.note: Retains enduring foliage but substitutes leaf retention for the stated absence of withering.

word_notes.lexical_gloss: And everything that he does succeeds or prospers.
word_notes.note: Extends the botanical metaphor while leaving the explicit claim about success in the person's actions unexpressed; blossoms are not mentioned.
